Antibacterial drug resistance is a problem in the manage- ment of gonococcal infection. Penicillins were once the treatment of choice for N. gonorrhoeae but are no longer recommended. High-level plasmid-mediated and chromo- somally mediated resistances have also been reported with tetracycline, and chromosomally mediated resistance to other antibiotics may occur. Gonococcal resistance is now monitored in England and Wales via the Gonococcal Re- sistance to Antimicrobials Surveillance Programme (GRASP)2 and in the USA by the Gonococcal Isolate Sur- veillance Project (GISP).3 Of concern are the increasing number of reports worldwide of resistance to fluoroqui- nolones which has resulted in revision of treatment guide- lines. In the UK fluoroquinolones are no longer recom- mended as first-line drugs, while in the USA they are no longer recommended for gonococcal infections. Infection with Chlamydia trachomatis (see under Chlamy- dial Infections, p.166) often occurs along with gonorrhoea and should be tested for or treated presumptively. Guidelines produced by WHO,4 by an expert group in the UK,5 and by the CDC in the USA1 for the treatment of gonorrhoea are as follows, although recommendations may need to be localised because of differences in patterns of infection and drug resistance: • UNCOMPLICATED ANOGENITAL GONOCOCCAL INFECTIONS IN ADULTS. • WHO: • a single oral dose of ciprofloxacin 500 mg, or • a single oral dose of cefixime 400 mg, or • a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone 125 mg, or • a single intramuscular dose of spectinomycin 2 g • UK: • a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone 250 mg, or • a single intramuscular dose of spectinomycin 2 g, or • a single oral dose of cefixime 400 mg alternative regimens are: • a single oral dose of ciprofloxacin 500 mg • a single oral dose of ofloxacin 400 mg • a single oral dose of ampicillin 2 or 3 g plus probenecid 1 g • a single intramuscular dose of cefotaxime 500 mg • a single intramuscular dose of cefoxitin 2 g plus oral probenecid 1 g • USA: • a single oral dose of cefixime 400 mg, or • a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone 125 mg Other single dose cephalosporins may be substituted.
